full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: This appeal by leave at the instance of the writ petitioner is directed against the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.50 of 1996 affirming those of the respondent No. 2 i.e. the Court of Settlement, in Case No. 11 of 1989 in respect of House No. 24/10, Block-C, Tajmahal Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. 

 2. The case of the appellant is that the case property previously belonged to Abdul Hafiz who got the same from the Government of the then East Pakistan by registered deed of lease dated 15-1-69 and constructed a tin shed house and lived there. The said Abdul Hafiz entered into an agreement on 20-12-71 with the appellant to sell the same to the appellant on receipt of Taka 13,500 as advance out of total consideration .money of Taka 15,000 and delivered possession of the same to the appellant on the same day as part performance of the agreement for sale Before the execution of the deed. Abdul Hafiz died in January 1972 leaving behind three legal heirs and successors namely, wife Hazera Khatun, daughter Baby Tabasun (minor) and son Md Kalim (minor). A succession certificate was issued in Succession Certificate Case No. 620 of 1978 by Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in support of aforesaid heirs and successors of deceased Abdul Hafiz. On 9-11-78 wife of deceased, Abdul Hafiz namely, Hazera Khatun, affirmed an affidavit before Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka declaring that she was a permanent resident of Bangladesh and also declared her intention to live in Bangladesh along with her entire family members for the remaining period of her life. On being refused by the successors of the deceased Abdul Hafiz on 20-11-78 to execute and register the deed of sale in respect of the suit property the appellant filed Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 before learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract in which respondent No: 2 Government of Bangladesh was. a party. The suit was decreed ex parte on 8-11-79 against which respondent No.2 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 187 of 1979 for setting aside the said, ex parte decree before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka who after hearing, by order dated 26-12-80 dismissed the case. Thereafter, the appellant filed Title Execution Case No.1 of 1981 before learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for execution of the said ex parte decree who after hearing by order dated 13-4-81 allowed the said execution case and executed and registered the deed of sale being No. 9921 dated 13- 4-81 in favour of the appellant. The appellant thereafter prayed for mutation of the property in his name to the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement Directorate of Housing and Urban Development. On 30-11-83, a high-powered survey team of the Ministry of Public Works after survey of the house made a report with the remark that the property might not be treated as an abandoned property. Thereafter, the Administrative Officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate sent a report dated 10-10-84 to the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement admitting the facts as stated with an observation that the appellant was in possession of the property by way of lawful purchase. Thereafter, the respondent No. 2 again filed Miscellaneous Case No. 183 of 1986 before learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for setting aside the aforesaid ex parte decree, which was dismissed for default on 7-2-89. The appellant claimed to have been in continuous peaceful possession of the suit property since 20-12-71 and was never dispossessed therefrom. The Government was never in possession of the property and the same was not leased out to anybody treating the same as an abandoned property at any point of time since 28-2-72. The appellant was surprised to know that the property was included in the "Ka" list as abandoned property by notification in the official Gazette on 28-11-85 under section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985. The appellant filed an application under said Ordinance to exclude the property from "Ka" list of abandoned properties before the Court of Settlement which after hearing the case dismissed the application with the findings that the whereabouts of the owner was not known, that he had been residing in a country which was at war with Bangladesh and that' the owner ceased to occupy, supervise or manage the property. 

 3. The appellant, being aggrieved by the judgment, filed the writ petition before the High Court Division which discharged the Rule upon finding, inter alia; that the appellant had filed only the photo copy of the lease deed of Abdul Hafiz and no other basic documents. The certified copy of the original deed was obtained on 22-8-78. He also did not file the deed of agreement for sale and simply said that he lost the agreement while returning from the Assistant Commissioner's Office on 25-10-84 after showing him all the documents. The Court of Settlement did not believe this story that he informed the police about it by filling an entry in the police diary. He produced a photo copy of the GDE which the Court of Settlement held was not proved by calling for Original from the police station. The record of the case was called from the Assistant Commissioner's Office where he filed all the photocopies except bainapatra and he did not complain about losing the bainapatra in the office of Housing and Settlement. With regard to the suit for specific performance of contract and execution of the registered, sale deed, the High Court Division referred to the case reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71 where it was held that in a suit for specific performance of contract the dispute between the vendor and the vendee is decided, and it does not exclude the property from being an abandoned property. Further, the appellant could not produce the sheet anchor of his claim i.e. the bainapatra, and "it is a mystery how the original succession certificate came to the hand of the petitioner where his claim was resisted by Abdul Hafiz". The High Court Division therefore, discharged the Rule. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider the point raised by the learned Counsel for the appellants that from the admitted position, apart from the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 that the petitioner is in possession of the property since 1978 and the possession having not been taken over by the Government, the listing of the property in "Ka" list is contrary to section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (LIV of 1985) and is illegal. The High Court Division failed to appreciate that the inclusion of the property in "Ka" list without any notice as contemplated under President's Order 16 of 1972 read with section 5 of the Ordinance LIV of 1985 was without lawful authority. It was further submitted that the case property 'being enlisted in the "Ka" list of the Gazette, although the petitioner had been on the property since 1971 on the strength of bainapatra and subsequent decree, and no notice having been given to the petitioner before enlisting of the properties in the Gazette, the inclusion of the case property in the list was without lawful authority and, in support, a decision of this Division in the case of Bangladesh vs Amena Khatun and others reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55 has been referred. 

 5. Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that from the admitted position that the appellant is in possession of the property since 17-12-1971 which he got from the admitted owner MA Hafiz, apart from the decree for specific performance of contract in Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 in which he obtained the registered deed executed and registered through Court, the possession not having been taken over by the Government, the listing of the property in 'Ka' schedule is contrary to the provision of section 5(1)(Ka) of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 (No. LIV of 1985). The learned Counsel has further submitted that after appropriate proceeding under Articles 7 and 15 of President's Order No.16 of 1972 and under section 5 of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985, the inclusion of the building in 'Ka' list without any notice as contemplated therein is illegal and is without any lawful authority: The learned Counsel has referred to the above decision in the case of Bangladesh vs Amena Khatun and others reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55. 

 7. Article 15 provides that any person claiming any right or interest may within 3 months of the announcing of the order claiming any interest or right therein treated by the Government as abandoned property may make an application stating that this property is not an abandoned property and his interest has not been affected by the provision of the said order. Admittedly, in the instant case no notice under Article 7 was served so as to entitle the appellant from challenging the order treating the property as abandoned. 

 8. Rule 5 of Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 as well provides that the property of which possession has already been taken by the Government as abandoned property could only be listed in the 'Ka' schedule under section 5(1)(a) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985, but in the instant case admittedly, the possession has been lying althrough with the appellant. The High Court. Division has not at all adverted its attention to the fact that according to clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Abandoned Property (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance 1985, abandoned property in possession of the Government could only be included in the "Ka" list of abandoned building in respect of which possession has been taken by issuance of notice under Article 7 of President's Order No.16 of 1972. 

 9. Although the appellant could not produce the bainapatra in original which the appellant is alleged to have lost and in support thereof had filed a GD. Entry but the said bainapatra was the subject-matter of Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 which was decreed ex parte and the appellant obtained document executed and registered through Court and the respondent No. 2 as well filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.183 of 1986 before the Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Dhaka for setting aside the aforesaid decree which was dismissed for default on 7-2-1989. Admittedly, the appellant has been claiming to be in continuous peaceful possession of the suit property since 20-12-1971 and was never dispossessed and he was also never issued with any notice to surrender. It further appears that the Government-respondents did not take any step to take over the possession of the same till publication of the Gazette notification on 23-9-1985. It further appears that even after publication of the Gazette notification the Government was aware of the decree in respect of the property in favour of the appellant and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 183 of 1986 before the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Dhaka for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 8-11-1979 in respect of the case building. Since there was no notice contemplated under Article 7 and there was non-compliance of the provision of section 5 of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 as no notice under section 5(1)(a) of the Ordinance was ever served and, as such, the property was wrongly included in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned buildings and the listing, as such, undoubtedly has been done illegally and without any lawful authority. This view finds support in the case referred to by the learned Counsel for the appellant in the case of Bangladesh vs Amena Khatun reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55.
